findings.observation: The relationship review presents a confirmed-state receipt, but the reviewed implementation only assigns an in-memory SwiftUI @State decision. It does not apply a typed, versioned canonical-state mutation or reload the changed state from a source of truth.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:11,61-78,461-495; apps/ios/UITests/CandidateSignalUITests.swift:44-48 asserts that the local receipt appears, not that canonical state changed; the frozen pnpm ios:check result exits 65.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter can be told that relationship state is confirmed even though dismissing or relaunching may discard the decision and Today may not reflect it, forcing reconciliation and undermining trust in the archive.
findings.recommendation: Either label this as a reversible local preview or connect confirmation to a typed, revision-checked canonical command whose receipt is re-read into Today; keep unresolved, conflict, retraction, and undo as explicit persisted states.
findings.verification: Confirm Leila's change, dismiss the sheet, relaunch the app, and return after a simulated day; the same revision and evidence-backed state must remain visible in Review and Today. Repeat with a concurrent revision and a retraction; no newer state may be overwritten.

findings.observation: The visible loop ends at reviewing a relationship-state label. It does not turn the unresolved client answer into a specific owned action, due condition, outcome receipt, or updated Pursuit progress, even though the design source defines that as the V1 job.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 screenshot ios-today-light.png sha256 4f4df9f8b9d5e1ce131c60b2881b6b400987ed3e960ad5ec341ae579a1984517 shows 'Review change' as the primary action; RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:46-93 ends with state confirmation; Decision Draft v2.0 sections 0.1, 3.2, 4.1, and 7.1 require Proposal -> Human Review -> Next Action -> Outcome around a Pursuit.
findings.user_impact: After spending attention on the review, the recruiter still has to remember what to ask, who owns it, when it is due, and where to record the result, so the product does not yet protect momentum better than a note or direct message.
findings.recommendation: After evidence review, stage one recruiter-owned action tied to the Chief Product Officer Pursuit, the client-policy gap, an owner, and a return condition; then show the observed result without sending externally.
findings.verification: Run the Leila scenario from Today through review and local action completion; a recruiter can identify the Pursuit outcome, blocking gap, owner, timing, evidence, and resulting progress without reconstructing context in another app.

findings.criterion: Pursuit-centered workflow and wedge discipline (rubric score 2)
findings.observation: The frozen build still uses Today, People, and Library and prioritizes relationship reminders. The Decision Draft v2.0 explicitly replaces that old direction with Today, Pursuits, and People, with goal risk, gaps, and actions preceding person-level detail.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 screenshot shows Today/People/Library; apps/ios/Sources/Features/RelationshipArchiveView.swift:64-79 switches among today, people, and library; lines 178-263 frame the main surface as two relationships requiring judgment; Decision Draft v2.0 sections 1.2, 6.1, 6.2, and 7.1 define the Pursuit-centered information architecture and exclude Library as a primary tab.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter handling several searches cannot compare which target outcome is most blocked or see how a person-level change affects a deadline, milestone, or resource gap; the user must mentally rebuild the business context.
findings.recommendation: Make Pursuit the navigation and decision context: replace Library as a primary tab with Pursuits, add target outcome/deadline/milestone/gap to Today focus, and route evidence through Pursuit, Person, Review, Inbox, and Search.
findings.verification: On a fixture with at least two live searches, Today ranks no more than three Pursuit focuses with goal, blocking gap, evidence freshness, and one action; opening each focus preserves the correct Pursuit and person context through Review.

findings.observation: Exact evidence, provenance, before/proposed values, Keep unresolved, and Confirm are coherently ordered, but the recruiter cannot edit the proposal, change its person/Pursuit association, or accept/reject individual changes before confirming.
findings.evidence: RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:17-59 and 83-93 renders evidence, provenance, and before/proposed state; lines 61-80 offers only package-level Keep unresolved or Confirm; CandidateSignalUITests.swift:23-48 checks evidence-before-decision and the receipt but no correction path.
findings.user_impact: A partially wrong interpretation forces the recruiter to leave the flow or keep everything unresolved, increasing abandonment or rubber-stamping risk.
findings.recommendation: Provide an in-context edit and association correction before confirmation, and let each proposed change be independently confirmed, removed, or kept unresolved while preserving the source excerpt.
findings.verification: Seed wrong identity, wrong Pursuit, and one incorrect proposed value; recruiters correct all three without accepting unrelated changes, and the audit record retains original proposal, correction, and evidence.

findings.criterion: Capture burden and complete-loop proof (rubric score 2)
findings.observation: The Today surface offers a compact capture entry, but the frozen executable result does not prove the capture-to-identity-to-reviewed-state loop because the relationship-capture UI test failed when its authorized localhost relationship fixture was unavailable.
findings.evidence: RelationshipArchiveView.swift:21-27 and 49-57 provides one-tap entry to CandidateSignalView; artifact.json frozen test result records pnpm ios:check exit 65, with 31 unit tests passing but CandidateSignalUITests.testRelationshipCaptureRequiresCurrentOwnerAndCompilesGoldWiki failing after the localhost relationship fixture was unavailable; external provider writes and recruiter field evidence are intentionally unavailable.
findings.user_impact: The evidence bundle cannot establish that capture is faster than the recruiter's manual fallback or that a captured conversation reliably returns to the correct person and search without recovery work.
findings.recommendation: Make the synthetic relationship fixture hermetic and run the complete capture, identity narrowing, evidence correction, confirmation, receipt, and Today projection path under interruption and offline recovery.
findings.verification: The frozen pnpm ios:check run passes from a clean environment, and a timed recruiter study compares input, context switches, correction burden, and time-to-useful-action against the existing manual workflow.

findings.criterion: Write safety and interruption recovery (rubric scores 2 and 2)
findings.observation: The UI states that no external system changed and offers Undo, but the current relationship decision has no visible idempotency, failure, retry, conflict, or durable day-return behavior. The separate resume surface asserts that edits are saved without demonstrating that it reloads the actual interrupted review.
findings.evidence: RelationshipArchiveSheets.swift:123-209 renders a generic resume screen; lines 461-495 renders the local receipt and Undo; RelationshipArchiveView.swift:68 selects a fixed resume person; the frozen UI tests include an in-process background test for TS-CORE-01 at CandidateSignalUITests.swift:311-322 but no force-quit/day-return test for RelationshipChangeReview.
findings.user_impact: A recruiter returning after interruption may see reassuring continuity copy without dependable restored work, and a failed or repeated confirmation cannot be safely reconciled.
findings.recommendation: Persist a review draft and operation ID, reload it by revision, and provide explicit pending, failed, unknown, conflict, retry, and reconciled states; only show saved/confirmed copy after reading the stored result.
findings.verification: Interrupt before and after confirmation by backgrounding, force-quitting, losing the response, and returning the next day; the app restores the exact review or reconciles one operation without duplicate state changes.

findings.observation: The lowest material dimensions are State integrity and Action usefulness, so the specialist score is 1 rather than an average of the polished and incomplete parts.
findings.evidence: TS-V1-BASELINE-20260824-01 dimension scores: Trigger relevance 3; Capture burden 2; Evidence review 2; State integrity 1; Action usefulness 1; Write safety 2; Interruption recovery 2; Wedge discipline 2. Scores use recruiter-workflow-reviewer/references/rubric.md and are tied to the frozen screenshot, source, design page, UI-test source, and failed pnpm ios:check receipt.
findings.user_impact: A decorative mean would overstate readiness and hide the two gaps most likely to waste recruiter time or create reconciliation work.
findings.recommendation: Retest the failed dimensions first; do not raise the overall specialist score until canonical state and one useful Pursuit action are proven end to end.
findings.verification: A comparable frozen artifact earns at least 3 in every material rubric dimension with a passing complete-loop receipt and no active veto.

strengths: Today clearly names why the Leila relationship returned to attention, shows recency, limits the visible queue, and explicitly treats no-action as a successful state.
The review source places exact evidence and provenance before the proposed change and offers Keep unresolved, a truthful no-external-effect boundary, and a visible Undo affordance.
The frozen screenshot has a quiet, legible hierarchy without candidate scores, risk meters, celebratory AI theater, or hidden automatic outreach.
missing_evidence: Real recruiter field evidence under realistic 5-20-search load, including a measured comparison with notes, ATS/CRM updates, and direct messaging; no proof is provided for time saved, momentum preserved, correction burden, or action completion.

A passing frozen end-to-end run from capture through deterministic identity binding, evidence correction, canonical state receipt, Pursuit action, Today update, and observed outcome; pnpm ios:check failed on the relationship-capture fixture.

Seeded ambiguity tests for wrong candidate or Pursuit, speaker/date/timezone ambiguity, no actionable signal, contradiction or retraction, expired deadline, and third-party personal information on the Pursuit-centered baseline.
Durable recovery evidence for app termination and next-day return, changed canonical state, confirmation failure, retry, unknown response reconciliation, duplicate prevention, and audit history.
Executable proof of the Decision Draft v2.0 Today/Pursuits/People information architecture, Pursuit Detail, Inbox, and a complete Proposal -> Review -> Action -> Outcome loop.
Production authentication, real-device behavior, production data, and external-provider writes were intentionally unavailable and therefore receive no credit.
open_questions: Is 'Relationship state confirmed' intentionally a synthetic local preview, or is it expected to represent a canonical internal write?
Which canonical entity and revision will own the Leila client-policy gap and its next action once Pursuit is implemented?
What field-study thresholds will define acceptable capture time, correction burden, review completion, stale-action rate, and verified Pursuit progress?
